kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: Beloved writer and environmentalist Wendell Berry has died at age 92
wire.summary: Wendell Berry has died at age 92 He was a beloved American poet, novelist, essayist, and farmer.

wire.title: SCOTUS allows Trump's ballroom project to continue. And, the Army secretary resigns
wire.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that President Trump's ballroom project may continue. And, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after 18 months on the job.

wire.title: They live by a shrine to a saint. Why are their homes being demolished?
wire.summary: The neighborhood is a pilgrimage site, with a shrine to the Sufi saint known as Bari Imam. In the past year, hundreds of homes of the working poor were razed. Residents fear more will be demolished.

wire.title: Why the Supreme Court's ballroom ruling could matter beyond the ballroom
wire.summary: Georgetown Law professor Stephen Vladeck explains the separation-of-powers questions raised by the Supreme Court's decision on the White House ballroom.

wire.title: Whistleblower claims USPS plan for Trump's mail voting order could 'derail' midterms
wire.summary: A whistleblower says the U.S. Postal Service is rushing out an online system for President Trump's push to restrict mail voting that could "derail" the midterm election if courts allow it to proceed.

wire.title: AI wealth is creating a 'mansion shortage' and upending San Francisco's housing market
wire.summary: Spiking prices and rental bidding wars are raising fears of more displacement in a city where previous tech booms and a housing shortage have already driven out many.

wire.title: A NY hospital tried to close its birthing center. This city united to fight back
wire.summary: Democrats and Republicans in Troy, New York, took on a national Catholic health system and kept the county's last birthing center open.

wire.title: A makeover for college: No gym, no meal plan and two years of work
wire.summary: A new model in Vermont emphasizes hands-on learning while stripping away frills like gyms and meal plans that increase costs. Other newly created institutions are also reimagining college.

wire.title: Judge to decide if Tyler Robinson will go to trial in Charlie Kirk murder case
wire.summary: Utah District Judge Tony Graf Jr. will hear arguments over evidence introduced in July, to decide if there's enough probable cause for a trial in the shooting of the conservative activist last year.

wire.title: 'It can outthink me': How a major manufacturer came to embrace AI
wire.summary: GE Appliances is leaning heavily into artificial intelligence to improve quality and efficiency on the factory floor.

wire.title: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack
wire.summary: A drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at the airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes on 4 August.

wire.title: 'I've never been to Afghanistan': Six million deportees forced to start over under the Taliban
wire.summary: As of August, the number forced to return this year from Pakistan and Iran had reached another million.

wire.title: River water smashed into tunnel and chased me for 20 minutes, Nepal worker tells BBC
wire.summary: Major efforts to rescue hydropower workers continue as Nepal's death toll exceeds 1,000.

wire.title: Sexual assaults happening almost every day in Ceuta, prosecutors say
wire.summary: Most migrants have returned to neighbouring Morocco, but as many as 5,000 remain in the Spanish exclave.

wire.title: Vance calls Michigan Senate candidate El-Sayed 'evil' at campaign rally
wire.summary: El-Sayed faces Trump ally Mike Rogers in what has quickly become a senate race characterised by personal attacks and insults between the two.

wire.title: Pistol in a lake gives hope for French cold case
wire.summary: Saad al-Hilli was shot dead with his wife and mother-in-law while holidaying in eastern France in September 2012.
